Vandita Jadeja

CRM
NOW
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

ServiceNow (NOW) trades at 27x forward earnings with 24% revenue growth, while Salesforce (CRM) delivers 11% growth at just 14x, forcing a speed-vs-value choice.

Despite ServiceNow's superior AI positioning, Salesforce's 7.34% free cash flow yield and $25B buyback slashing shares from 962M to 821M tip the author's pick.

ServiceNow's AI Control Tower already manages agents across rival platforms, and its CRM business has grown into a $2B ACV operation encroaching on Salesforce's core turf.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) and Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) both reported this summer with the same message: agentic AI is now showing up in bookings. They differ sharply on price.

Pixels Hunter / Shutterstock.com

ServiceNow grew revenue 24% and trades at 27x forward earnings. Salesforce grew 10.8% at about 14x. So investors have to pick between speed and value.

Governance Sells at ServiceNow While Salesforce Customers Keep Refilling the Tank

ServiceNow's subscription revenue reached $3.877B, up 24.5%. That is rare speed at this scale. Its AI annual contract value (ACV) passed $1B. More than 500 customers went live on AI Control Tower within six months.

That product manages AI agents across other vendors' platforms, which puts ServiceNow in charge of everyone else's AI. The CFO summed up the pitch: "Customers aren't paying us for tokens, they're paying for resolutions." ServiceNow is also moving onto Salesforce's territory.

NOW Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.

Salesforce's current remaining performance obligations (cRPO, or contracted revenue due within 12 months) rose 14%, up from 13% last quarter. The backlog is starting to speed up again. Agentforce annual recurring revenue exceeded $1.5B, and 50% of bookings came from customers buying more credits. That points to real usage beyond pilot projects.

I remain skeptical of the headline earnings, though. Non-GAAP EPS of $5.90 included about $2.53/share from investment profits. The Informatica acquisition also added $456M in revenue.

title: Is Salesforce (CRM) Cheap After AIforce And Koa Launches?
detail:
Is Salesforce (CRM) Cheap After AIforce And Koa Launches?
Bailey Pemberton
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 10:07 AM MDT 3 min read
CRM
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce, the US software group behind a broad suite of CRM and AI tools, has seen a mixed share price ride in recent years, which raises a simple question for you as an investor: Is the current US$234.02 price adequately backed by the earnings power the company is generating today?

Over the past 3 years, Salesforce shares have delivered a 17.1% gain, so anyone buying in now needs to judge whether the underlying earnings profile still matches that kind of performance.

Fresh AI launches like the AIforce platform and the Koa reasoning model, along with security fixes around reported SalesBleed vulnerabilities, can shape how investors think about future profitability, investment needs, and the pace at which earnings may be reinvested into growth.

The analysts covering Salesforce have run their own numbers. See what analysts think Salesforce's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether Salesforce's current share price is adequately supported by its earnings when set against the Fair Ratio benchmark.

If you are comparing Salesforce with other AI focused software companies using the same earnings perspective, it can help to examine that Fair Ratio question across 38 AI small caps.

Is Salesforce Still Cheap on Earnings?

The P/E ratio fits Salesforce because earnings are a key focus for investors watching how the CRM and AI bets translate into profit. On this measure, Salesforce trades at about 19.9x earnings, which is below both the wider software industry average of roughly 29.7x and the peer group level near 42.4x. The Fair Ratio model, which blends factors like growth profile, margins, size and risk into an implied multiple, points to a higher figure than the current P/E. On this framework, the stock screens as undervalued rather than stretched.

Despite the recent AIforce and Koa launches lifting interest in Salesforce as an AI platform, the valuation still lags the peer average, which already prices in richer expectations for many software stocks. For you as a shareholder or potential buyer, the gap between Salesforce's 19.9x and these benchmarks suggests the market is not assigning the same earnings multiple as comparable software groups. You would need to decide whether that discount reflects risk concerns or an opportunity. Explore the numbers behind Salesforce's P/E valuation.

Why Salesforce, ServiceNow and Snowflake All Dropped 4% Within Minutes of a Meta Announcement Monday
Joel South

META
CRM
NOW
SNOW
MDB
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Meta's WhatsApp agents already handle sales and service conversations, making Salesforce the most direct target; both Salesforce and ServiceNow dropped 4-5% within minutes.

MongoDB plunged 21% after Meta hired its CEO as chief enterprise platform officer, while Meta itself fell 4% despite holding a $1.59 trillion market cap.

Zuckerberg called enterprise 'a somewhat different muscle' for Meta, which has yet to name a single customer or publish pricing for the new platform.

Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

At 8:36 AM ET this morning, Meta (NASDAQ:META) published "Meta launches enterprise platform, MongoDB CEO exits" to its newsroom, confirming it hired MongoDB (NASDAQ:MDB) CEO CJ Desai as chief enterprise platform officer. Enterprise software repriced within minutes. Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) fell 4.23% to $224.13, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) fell 4.99% to $128.85 and Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW) fell 4.06% to $322.30. MongoDB dropped 20.9% to $324.54.

clasesdeperiodismo / BY-SA 2.0

The buyer got punished too. Meta slipped 3.97% to $721.83, four days after a 52-week high of $777.59 on Sept. 24, 2026.

What the Event Actually Covers

Two things are confirmed: the platform launch and the Desai hire. Everything else is intent. Available disclosures attach no pricing, customer list or revenue target to the platform, so none is assumed here.

The best map of scope is Meta's July 29, 2026 earnings call. Mark Zuckerberg, CEO at the time of that call, said "we see a large enterprise opportunity to sell to businesses, including APIs, business agents, and many more." He described pricing as "a mix of subscriptions, volume-based pricing" plus results-based fees. Meta business agents already serve more than 1 million businesses weekly on WhatsApp and Messenger.

Who Gets Hurt, Sized Against Their Businesses

Meta carries a $1.59 trillion market cap and booked $59.36B in Q2 advertising revenue. Enterprise revenue is undisclosed and, for now, a rounding error beside the ad engine. The spending is concrete: 2026 capex guidance of $130-145B.

Taken together, the three moves show how quickly one announcement can reset expectations across the enterprise software sector.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is down only 1%, a modest decline next to the individual names. Over in large-cap tech, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is also down 1%.
